harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created appworker account on node1 and configured PAM limits (8192 open files, 256 processes) for its login sessions via /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf; verified enforcement with a login shell. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id/uptime, rebooted node1 via systemd-run, confirmed boot_id changed after reconnecting, and re-verified the account/limits config and enforcement post-restart.
actions_performed: Checked OS and confirmed appworker did not already exist on node1
Wrote /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf with soft/hard nofile=8192 and soft/hard nproc=256
Verified limits took effect via 'sudo su - appworker' ulimit checks
Captured baseline boot_id and uptime before restart
Scheduled and executed a reboot via systemd-run --on-active=1 systemctl reboot
Polled node1 until it reconnected and confirmed boot_id changed
Re-verified appworker account, limits config file, and enforced ulimits post-restart

evidence.summary: Confirmed no pre-existing appworker user, then created it via useradd -m; id shows uid=1000(appworker)

evidence.requirement: Login sessions limited to 8192 open files and 256 processes
evidence.summary: Wrote limits.d drop-in with nofile=8192 and nproc=256 (soft/hard), then confirmed via 'sudo su - appworker' that ulimit -n returns 8192 and ulimit -u returns 256
Captured boot_id bf4e9cbb-84f9-45f0-9b81-6602b98cea07, uptime since 2026-09-29 10:40:29, and confirmed appworker account and limits.d config present
systemd-run scheduled 'systemctl reboot' 1s in the future and returned the timer/service unit names immediately

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: After reconnecting, boot_id is now 3e520be2-146e-4d85-9f6d-681b2dad3d49 (different from baseline) with fresh uptime since 2026-09-29 10:42:12, proving an actual reboot occurred
After restart, appworker account still exists, limits.d/appworker.conf content is intact, and a login shell for appworker still reports ulimit -n=8192 and ulimit -u=256
